clue.text: Against sweets being shown as evil things

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against
ices are frozen desserts, sweets after a meal

explanation.surface: Puddings are being condemned as wicked indulgences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being shown as' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vices are moral failings, wicked habits.

clue.text: The companion-help

parts.note: a handy reference book carried about, Latin for 'go with me'

explanation.surface: A helper who keeps one company.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbook or guide kept always at hand.

clue.text: A disheartening device

parts.note: read 'disheartening' literally: a gadget that removes the middle of fruit

explanation.surface: Something that saps one's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartening' means taking the heart (core) out of an apple, not depressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool for removing the centre of apples.

clue.text: A foreigner catches up around here in France

indicators.note: the turned word goes round the French word
in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to nail a culprit is to catch him
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: An alien collars people somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NAILS into SLIAN, and 'around' puts it round ICI.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Italian island is a foreigner to the British.

clue.text: Unwillingly late

parts.note: read 'unwillingly' as 'without a will' and 'late' as 'dead': someone who died leaving no will

explanation.surface: Someone turned up behind time and did so grudgingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests reluctant tardiness; 'late' here means deceased and 'unwillingly' means having made no will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies without having made a legal will is said to have died in that state.

clue.text: Some will never ride again fancy!

indicators.note: only some of the letters are taken, a run inside the words 'ride again'

explanation.surface: A rider who has fallen vows not to mount again, imagine!
explanation.walkthrough: 'will never' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or thought.

clue.text: Sound footwork

parts.note: dance steps made audible by metal-tipped shoes

explanation.surface: Competent movement of the feet, as in boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' suggests solid or reliable; it means noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancing in shoes with metal plates that click on the floor.

clue.text: Not entirely honest about mid-morning drink

indicators.note: the word for dishonest goes round the other piece

parts.note: shady means dubious, not quite honest

indicators.note: mid points to the central letter of the word 'morning'

explanation.surface: A slightly dodgy elevenses tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-morning' hides the centre of 'morning', its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a light drink.

clue.text: Set against a tall team

parts.note: long means tall, lengthy
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A lofty squad is placed in opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed beside or next to something, so set in comparison.

clue.text: Better people interrupt: a top journalist

indicators.note: one word breaks into the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the top newspaper journalist
men means people

explanation.surface: Others cut in on a senior newspaperman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb meaning improve.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or improve a text.

clue.text: Third pace maker that's quite inexpensive

indicators.note: a maker builds something new, so the letters of the two preceding words are rebuilt into fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone who sets the pace and finishes third comes at little cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pace maker' looks like a runner, but 'maker' is the anagram signal, rearranging THIRD and PACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going for next to nothing is very cheap, as cheap as soil.

clue.text: A poem by a nautical man called "Home"

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece stands beside the other

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A sailor has written verse with the title 'Home'.
explanation.walkthrough: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a standard crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling, the place where one lives.

clue.text: Added about a pound for the spirit

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: more means additional, extra
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone tacked on roughly a pound to pay for drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests liquor in the surface; it means the mood of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the confidence and enthusiasm of a team, its collective spirit.

clue.text: Players old? Bound to be

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
aged means old

explanation.surface: Are the musicians elderly? Surely they must be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be' reads as 'certain to be'; 'Bound' is the past participle of bind, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound that has been bound up has been dressed with strips of cloth.

clue.text: Connection of capital with pawnbroker

parts.note: capital as an exclamation means excellent, great
uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker

explanation.surface: A link between a city and a moneylender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is the old exclamation of approval; 'Uncle' is old British slang for the pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's uncle is a relation, a family connection.

clue.text: Prepare to fire a second fabulous monster

parts.note: to cock a gun is to raise its hammer ready for firing
a trice is an instant, as in 'in a trice'

explanation.surface: Get the gun ready again, then shoot at a mythical beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means belonging to fable rather than wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary serpent hatched from a cock's egg, able to kill with a glance.

clue.text: Opposing a man playing cricket in Advent

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for arrival

parts.note: advent means arrival, coming
a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A man plays cricket in the weeks before Christmas, against opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advent' is not the Christmas season here but an arrival; BAT is a cricket term for a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting against, resisting.

clue.text: Beware of the intellectual!

definitions.meaning: as in 'watch out for the step!' as a command to take care
a great thinker can be called a brilliant brain

explanation.surface: A warning to steer clear of the clever person.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means take care about; as a noun it names a gifted thinker or the intellect itself.

clue.text: Finds a record past bearing

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means finished, past
S, south, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Someone digs out an old disc showing the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To find is to come upon, to uncover.

clue.text: Not the speediest way to Scotland!

definitions.text: Not the speediest way to Scotland!

parts.words: Not the speediest way to Scotland!
parts.note: the song 'Loch Lomond': the one taking the low road gets to Scotland first

explanation.surface: A remark on a slow route north.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'Loch Lomond', 'You take the high road and I'll take the low road, and I'll be in Scotland afore ye.'
explanation.definitionFit: A main road, here the slower route of the Scottish song.

clue.text: Say nothing, but act

parts.note: a performer who silently conveys a story by gesture alone

explanation.surface: Advice to keep quiet and get on with doing something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as advice to stop talking and take action; 'act' means perform on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Silent performance using only gesture and expression.

clue.text: Aid's sent in for distribution — nice quality

indicators.note: distributing aid spreads it around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Relief supplies have been dispatched to be handed out, a pleasing thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nice' here means delicate or refined, its older sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicacy and refinement in manner or appearance is a fine, nice quality.

clue.text: Cutting the man taking flight

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
wing means to fly, as in 'winging'

explanation.surface: A man runs off with a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping with an axe or blade.

clue.text: High-rise flats (numbered with a cross here)

definitions.text: High-rise flats (numbered with a cross here)

parts.words: High-rise flats (numbered with a cross here)
parts.note: elevated level stretches of land, in the plural form that ends with the letter shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: Tower blocks marked with an X on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-rise flats' suggests tower blocks; it means raised flat land, and the cross is the X of the French-style plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Tablelands are elevated level areas, raised flat ground.

clue.text: Craves soft illumination

parts.note: p, piano, is soft in music
rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Someone longs for gentle lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Craves in the old sense of begs, entreats.

clue.text: Very occupied by intimate Eastern cult

indicators.note: one word is filled by another, so the second goes inside the first

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
to intimate is to suggest indirectly, to hint

explanation.surface: A deeply private Oriental sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intimate' looks like an adjective for a close-knit cult; it is the verb meaning hint.
explanation.definitionFit: The native religion of Japan, worshipping kami spirits.

clue.text: If one is upset a row can result

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Disturbing someone may lead to an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A row is a din, a loud racket.

clue.text: A boy with nothing inside him as it's early

indicators.note: the zero goes within the word for a boy

parts.note: a son is a boy
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A lad with an empty stomach because it is morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Before long, shortly, at an early time.

clue.text: Elsewhere defence may 'be offered

parts.note: a plea in court that the accused was in some other place, from the Latin word meaning elsewhere

explanation.surface: Some other place may put up resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word for 'elsewhere' became the English name for this defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim that the accused was somewhere else when the crime happened.

clue.text: He used the Nile for self-improvement, said Carroll

definitions.text: He used the Nile for self-improvement, said Carroll

parts.words: He used the Nile for self-improvement, said Carroll
parts.note: Lewis Carroll's verse 'How doth the little...' has a reptile improve its shining tail with the waters of the Nile

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll reports someone who bettered himself by the Egyptian river.
explanation.walkthrough: The allusion is to Lewis Carroll's 'Alice' parody of 'How doth the little busy bee'.
explanation.definitionFit: The large reptile of Carroll's poem pours river water over its scales.

clue.text: Discerning man with fresh colour

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
green means new, inexperienced, fresh

explanation.surface: A perceptive fellow with a healthy complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: A greyish-green shade like the herb's leaves.

clue.text: Deck — there are many about an ocean-going vessel

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number
re means concerning, about
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: On a ship's deck there are plenty of people around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there are' only links; 'Deck' is the verb meaning adorn, not part of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to adorn, as one may array a ship with flags.
